deliverables_scope.text: ===== FILE: files/Attachment_1_-_Disintegrator_Salient_Characteristics_Rev1.pdf ===== Item: Solid State Disintegrator Quantity: 1 Item Description: Must ensure the disintegrator meets requirements set by the National Security Agency (NSA)/Central Security Service (CSS) for sanitization of classiﬁed solid state storage devices. Essential Salient Characteristics for Solid State Disintegrator: • Device must have simple, automatic push-button operation • Device must have an internal sensor to sense overload and must be able to reverse automatically to clear and prevent jams. • Device must have an automatic bin-full sensor • Device must have life-extend destruction blades, grinders and screens that must be easily reused, adjusted and replaced • Device acous

Strip Cards. Additional information: Contractor must install disintegrator and ensure it is fully functional. Contractor must provide twelve (12) disposable disintegrator bags, one (1) extra set of castor wheels (if disintegrator is on wheels)/feet, and necessary cleaning tools to maintain cleanliness to disintegrator. ===== FILE: files/Attachment_2_-_NSA_EPL_Devices_Apr2026.pdf ===== UNCLASSIFIED April 2026 Page 1 NSA/CSS EPL-Solid State Disintegrators UNCLASSIFIED NSA/CSS Evaluated Products List for Solid State Sanitization Devices OVERVIEW Devices included on this list have passed evaluation by meeting requirements set by the NSA/CSS for the sanitization of classified solid state storage devices. Meant to serve as guidance, inclusion in this document is not an endorsement by the NSA/CSS or the U.S. Government. All listed products sanitize TS/SCI and below. The NSA/CSS conducts continuous research on data recovery and data sanitization. This document is updated on an as-needed basis. The procedures for administration and distribution of the EPL are subject to change without notice. Please see Expired Products list for more information about removed products. Questions about specific models can be directed to the Center for Storage Device Sanitiz

id state storage devices. Meant to serve as guidance, inclusion in this document is not an endorsement by the NSA/CSS or the U.S. Government. All listed products sanitize TS/SCI and below. The NSA/CSS conducts continuous research on data recovery and data sanitization. This document is updated on an as-needed basis. The procedures for administration and distribution of the EPL are subject to change without notice. Please see Expired Products list for more information about removed products. Questions about specific models can be directed to the Center for Storage Device Sanitization Research at 301-688-1053 or CSDSR_NSA@nsa.gov. REQUIREMENTS SUMMARY The device must reduce any solid state storage device to a maximum edge size of 2 millimeter or less. Not all devices can securely disintegrate all solid state storage devices. Be sure to review the “acceptable material” remarks for approved formats. Inclusion in this list does not guarantee the continued performance of equipment. Customers should re-test equipment according to manufacturer guidance. Examples of solid state storage devices include: • Cell Phones • Tablets • USB/Flash/Thumb Drives • Solid State Drives inside Desktop Computers and Laptops • Circuit Boards • Cards Storage Devices Include: SIM

xamples of solid state storage devices include: • Cell Phones • Tablets • USB/Flash/Thumb Drives • Solid State Drives inside Desktop Computers and Laptops • Circuit Boards • Cards Storage Devices Include: SIM Cards, EMV Cards, Credit Cards and other Magnetic Strip Cards • Optical Storage Devices include: CDs, DVDs and Blu-ray Disks (BD) IMPORTANT REMINDERS This list serves as guidance for the sanitization of solid state and optical devices. Remove all labels or markings that indicate previous use or classification. Each device offers different convenience features, capacities, feed sizes, footprints and power requirements. Contact the vendor to identify the unit(s) best suited to your site’s needs. Equipment is listed in alphabetical order by vendor. Models that are no longer manufactured but still approved are included as well. Model numbers on equipment must match the model numbers shown in this list. Alternate or previously used retail names appear in parentheses. Fiscal Year 2026. (c) Solicitation number. Not applicable. (h) Background information about the requirement. DHS/CBP, Air and Marine Operations (AMO) has the responsibility to secure the Nation’s borders a

MSS operational sites, and four TAS operational sites. All sites require gaseous helium, which is stored in helium tube trailers onsite. Helium provides direct lift aerial support to Aerostat, radar, and other surveillance tools to overcome line of sight constraints to deter illegal activity along the U.S Southern Border, Florida Keys, and portions of the Caribbean. The trailers used to store and provide helium are required to be recertified every 5-10 years to comply with U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) Pipeline and Material Safety regulations. Currently, CBP Aerostats have thirty (30) trailers, six (6) of which are out of certification or near the end of their certification periods. Recertification will avoid disruption of site operations that could result in site Non-Mission Capability (NMC) and create a potential national security risk. CBP requires trailer support to ensure 24/7/365 continuous operations and maintenance of TARS operational sites. Due to the potential national security risk, critical nature of this requirement, timeline, resources, and cost, CBP requires a vendor that can meet the minimum requirements to recertify helium trailers and ensure continuation of TARS operations across the fleet. Section 5 – Scope of Work The contractor shall pick up student laundry bags six days per week, Monday through Saturday, from three designated campus locations; process the laundry at the contractor’s off-site facility; and return finished laundry in accordance with the schedule in Section 8. The Government does not provide laundry bags. The Government will provide an on-campus storage area with reasonable shelving for finished laundry. The contractor shall manually move laundry bags as necessary, including movement over stairs at designated pickup or delivery locations, and shall provide continuous on-site staffing to monitor student retrieval of completed laundry between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. The objective is to provide convenient student access and prevent misappropriation of laundry bags. For general planning purposes, the estimated scale of operations is approximately 4,000 pounds of laundry per week. This estimate is not a guaranteed minimum or maximum quantity. Historical daily, monthly, annual, seasonal, location- specific, or July surge-volume data is not maintained by the Government.
